root_cause.text: The `sev_ioctl_do_get_id2()` function in the CCP driver copies the ID blob to userspace even when the PSP firmware command fails, allowing an oversized copy that reads beyond the kernel-allocated buffer and leaks data.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an error check (`if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error)) goto e_free;`) after the `__sev_do_cmd_locked()` call to prevent the copy to userspace when the command fails. The KASAN report shows a slab-out-of-bounds read in `copy_to_user` where the copy size (`data.len`) was set by the firmware to a value larger than the kernel buffer, as described in the CVE.

Author: Sean Christopherson <seanjc@google.com>

    crypto: ccp: Use the stack for small SEV command buffers
    
    For commands with small input/output buffers, use the local stack to

bic_trace_step.reason: The function `sev_ioctl_do_get_id2` (shown in the diff) contains the vulnerable construct: after calling `__sev_do_cmd_locked(SEV_CMD_GET_ID, &data, &argp->error)`, the code unconditionally copies data to userspace without checking the return value `ret`. Specifically, after line `ret = __sev_do_cmd_locked(...)`, the code sets `input.length = data.len;` and then calls `copy_to_user` for `input` and also for `id_blob` using `data.len` as the size. If the firmware command fails but still modifies `data.len` (e.g., to a larger value), the subsequent `copy_to_user` may read beyond the allocated `id_blob` buffer, leading to an information leak. The fix (checking `ret` before copying) is not present in this commit.
